intro: High in the Latmos mountains, a sacred road climbs from Mylasa towards the god of the sky. You have arrived at Labraunda, the Sanctuary of Zeus Labraundos, in Muğla province. Its story reaches back to the 7th century BC, and this mountain sanctuary was always bound to Mylasa by that sacred road. Shall we walk it together?
history: The earliest finds here date to around 600 BC. Then, in the 4th century BC, came the Hecatomnid rulers: Mausolus and his brother Idrieus. They transformed Labraunda into a splendid cult centre, raising the Temple of Zeus, banqueting halls called androns, stoas and monumental gateways, the propylaia. The sanctuary remained in use in Roman times, and the cult endured until a Byzantine church was built on the site.
structure-2: You are now standing before Andron A, one of the banquet halls of Labraunda. Pause for a moment and imagine the guests gathering inside, the feast about to begin.
structure-3: And here is Andron B, the second banquet hall of Labraunda. Two halls built for feasting in one mountain sanctuary: here, worship and the banquet went hand in hand.
structure-4: Now look at the South Propylon, the monumental gateway at the south of the sanctuary. Picture yourself passing through it: this was a threshold, the moment a visitor stepped onto sacred ground.
structure-5: Next comes the Oikoi Building, a ceremonial building made up of small chambers. Its rooms are modest in size, yet each of them served the ceremonies of Labraunda.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Temple of Zeus, the god whose sanctuary this was.
facts: Did you know? Zeus Labraundos was shown holding a double-headed axe, the labrys, and the word 'labyrinth' shares the same root. The sanctuary owes its splendour to the Carian satrap Mausolus and his brother Idrieus: this was the mountain temple of the very dynasty that raised the Mausoleum. A fourteen-kilometre Sacred Way linked it to Mylasa, and we know the procession climbed it on foot. And its andrones, the royal banqueting halls, are the best-preserved examples known anywhere in the Greek world.
outro: This brings our journey through Labraunda, the Sanctuary of Zeus Labraundos to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
